purpose: Brentuximab vedotin is used to treat certain types of lymphoma, which is a cancer that starts in the lymph system. It is commonly used for Hodgkin lymphoma and a type called anaplastic large cell lymphoma. It may be used when other treatments have not worked or as part of initial treatment in some cases.
how_it_works: Think of this medicine as a smart missile that seeks out and destroys cancer cells. It is made up of an antibody (a protein that finds cancer cells) attached to a powerful chemotherapy drug. The antibody homes in on a specific protein called CD30 found on certain cancer cells, delivers the chemotherapy directly inside those cells, and kills them — while trying to leave healthy cells alone.
common_side_effects: Nerve tingling, numbness, or pain in hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy), nausea, tiredness and fatigue, fever, diarrhea, decreased appetite, hair loss, low blood counts (which can increase infection risk and cause bruising or bleeding), and rash.
warnings: This medication can cause serious nerve damage that may become permanent — tell your doctor right away if you feel numbness, tingling, or weakness. It can severely lower your blood counts, increasing your risk of life-threatening infections. Rare but serious lung problems can occur. It may cause liver problems, so your liver will be monitored. It can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is very important during and after treatment. Avoid live vaccines during therapy.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV infusion (into a vein) at a clinic or infusion center, usually once every 3 weeks. Each treatment session takes about 30 minutes. Your doctor will determine the exact dose based on your body weight and the type of lymphoma being treated. Your dosing schedule may be adjusted depending on how your body responds to the medication.
